title: Structured triage lattice for high-risk security asks
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Design and deliver a repeatable, explainable triage lattice that routes incoming enterprise security and compliance requests (SOC2/ISO attestations, HIPAA/DPA questions, GDPR data-subject flows, vendor questionnaires) into prioritized lanes with clear SLAs, remediation playbooks, and ownership.

Background: We receive a rising volume of customer security asks with inconsistent metadata (spreadsheet questionnaires, ad-hoc emails, legal templates). Current triage is manual, slow, and loses context across handoffs. This ticket defines a structured scoring lattice that combines risk signals, deployment constraints (hosted/dedicated/private), requested evidence, and business priority to output: priority lane, SLA, required artifact list, and an initial responder assignment.

Scope:
- Inbound channels: support portal, salesperson intake form, security@, and account manager attachments.
- Scoring signals: data types involved, retention/residency constraints, regulatory scope, contract phase, requested artifacts, and customer tier.
- Outputs: lane (fast-track / standard / programmatic-remediation / escalation), SLA target, list of evidence templates, suggested automation (LLM-assisted answers, evidence bundler).

Non-goals: automated full answers to questionnaires; replacing legal review for contract changes; auto-approving high-risk requests.

Deliverables:
1) Scoring lattice definition doc (Confluence) with weights and rationale.
2) Prototype intake form + sample mappings.
3) Decision table mapping to lanes and SLA commitments.
4) Implementation stub for triage classifier (ENG handoff) and acceptance test harness.
5) Playbooks for each lane with handoff steps and draft email templates.

Acceptance criteria:
- Lattice doc approved by Security & GTM (signoffs captured in Confluence).
- Prototype maps 100 historical requests and matches retrospective priority > 85% against manually labeled set.
- SLA definitions cover 95% of request types and include escalation windows.
- Clear owner for each lane and automation suggestions annotated with estimated engineering effort.

Success metrics: mean time to first response (MTTR) for high-risk asks reduced by 40% in first quarter post-launch; per-request routing accuracy >= 85%; time-to-evidence-bundle <= 3 business days for standard lane.

Notes / trade-offs: prefer explainability over marginal accuracy; initial lattice will be rule-based with a lightweight ML scorer in next phase. Keep customer-facing language generic; sensitive artifact names restricted to internal Confluence.
